mainTopic: Partial and uncertain awareness of impurity in the מקדש, the end of פרק ידיעות הטומאה, and the opening of פרק שבועות שתים on oaths about eating.
overview: A person walked on two paths. One of them was definitely impure, but nobody knows which one, and he entered the מקדש after walking on them. רבא explains that the dispute about the first case depends on whether partial awareness (מקצת ידיעה) counts as full awareness. In the case where he purified himself between the two paths, the first תנא still makes him liable. רבי יוחנן says that here uncertain awareness (ספק ידיעה) was treated like real awareness. ריש לקיש says the ברייתא follows רבי ישמעאל, who needs no awareness at the beginning. The גמרא then shows that each of them seems to say the reverse in their readings of רבי's view on eating possible חלב. It resolves both contradictions: טומאת מקדש is a special case, and ריש לקיש chose רבי ישמעאל to teach that he needs no awareness at the beginning even from tradition. After the הדרן, a new פרק opens with four kinds of oaths about eating and רבי עקיבא's ruling that any amount breaks a 'not eat' oath. The גמרא then begins to discuss what 'שבועה שאוכל' means, and אביי's answer continues on the next עמוד.

steps.title: How can he be exempt when he walked both paths?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the version of רבי שמעון's opinion that exempts the person even in the first case, where he walked both paths without purifying in between.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even in the first case, he is exempt?! Either way, he is impure!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is surprised that רבי שמעון would exempt the person even when he walked on both paths without purifying in between. Whichever path was the impure one, he walked on it, so he is surely impure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When he walks both paths with no purification between them, there is no doubt left: one of the two paths was impure, so he definitely became טמא. Exempting him from a קרבן seems to make no sense.

keyTerms.meaning: The first case: walking both paths without purifying in between
Whichever way you look at it; either way
Ritually impure

phrases.english: And even in the first case?!
phrases.notes: He means: does רבי שמעון really exempt him even when he walked both paths, one after the other?

phrases.english: Whichever way you look at it, he is impure!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the version from earlier in the sugya that says רבי שמעון exempts him even in the first case.
steps.kashyaTarget: The version that says רבי שמעון exempts him even when there was no purification between the two paths.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Whichever path was the impure one, he definitely walked on it, so his impurity is certain and he should be liable.

steps.title: רבא: he forgot the first path, so his awareness was only partial
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that the case is one where he forgot the first path while walking the second, so his lapse of awareness covered only part of the facts.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Here we are dealing with a case where he walked on the first path, and when he walked on the second path he forgot that he had walked on the first. So he had only partial awareness.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the question by describing a specific case. While walking on the second path, the person forgot about the first path.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When he entered the מקדש, he was missing awareness of only one path. That path alone is only a doubt, so this counts as partial awareness (מקצת ידיעה), not clear knowledge of definite impurity. That is why רבי שמעון could exempt him.

keyTerms.meaning: What case are we dealing with here? (used to narrow down the case)
He forgot
Partial awareness: knowing only part of what makes him definitely impure

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think he forgot that he was impure in general. He forgot only that he had walked on the first path, and that path by itself is only a doubt.

phrases.english: Rava said:
Here, what are we dealing with?
A case where he walked on the first path,
and at the time he walked on the second,
he forgot that he had walked on the first;
so that it is, for him, only partial awareness.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 1 by narrowing the case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: He knew about both paths, so his impurity was definite and known.
steps.terutzMaskana: He forgot the first path, so at the moment he entered he had only partial awareness of his impurity.

steps.title: The dispute: does partial awareness count as full awareness?
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that the two versions of רבי שמעון's opinion disagree about whether partial awareness counts as full awareness.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this is what they disagree about. The first תנא holds that we say partial awareness is like full awareness. רבי שמעון holds that we do not say partial awareness is like full awareness.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא finishes his answer by naming the exact point of disagreement between the two versions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to the first תנא, partial awareness counts as full awareness, so the person is liable in the first case. The other version, in the name of רבי שמעון, holds that partial awareness does not count, so he is exempt even in the first case.

keyTerms.meaning: This is the point they disagree about
The first תנא, whose view is stated first
Like full awareness

steps.whatToRemember: The question of whether מקצת ידיעה counts like full ידיעה is what decides the first case.

phrases.english: And this is what they disagree about:
The first tanna holds:
We say partial awareness is like full awareness;
and Rabbi Shimon holds:
phrases.notes: This is the version that reports רבי שמעון as exempting even in the first case, which is רבי שמעון בן יהודה's report.

phrases.aramaic: לָא אָמְרִינַן מִקְצָת יְדִיעָה כְּכׇל יְדִיעָה.
phrases.english: We do not say partial awareness is like full awareness.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רבא's answer by naming the principle that each side holds.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifying the underlying principle of the dispute
steps.terutzMaskana: The first תנא says partial awareness counts as full awareness; the other version says it does not.

steps.title: The case where he purified between the two paths
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next case of the ברייתא: he walked the first path and entered, purified himself, then walked the second path and entered again.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he walked on the first path and entered, then was sprinkled, sprinkled again, and immersed, and then walked on the second path and entered, he is liable. רבי שמעון exempts him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings up the next case in the ברייתא. It is setting up the question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here he fully purified himself between the two paths. So each time he entered, it is unclear whether he was impure at that moment. Still, the first תנא makes him liable.

keyTerms.meaning: He was sprinkled with the purifying waters
He did it again (a second sprinkling)
He immersed in a מקוה
Exempts

phrases.english: If he walked on the first path and entered,
was sprinkled, and again, and immersed,
phrases.notes: This is the full purification from impurity of a dead body: sprinkling on day three and day seven, then immersion.

phrases.english: then went back and walked on the second and entered —
he is liable, and Rabbi Shimon exempts him.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָלַךְ בָּרִאשׁוֹן וְנִכְנַס, הִזָּה וְשָׁנָה וְטָבַל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the first case to the second case of the ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If he purified between the two paths, the first תנא makes him liable and רבי שמעון exempts him.

steps.title: Why liable, when each entry was only a doubt?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the first תנא makes him liable, since each entry involved only uncertain awareness.
steps.simpleTranslation: But why is he liable? It is only uncertain awareness!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the first תנא's ruling of חייב in the second case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On the first entry, maybe that path was clean. On the second entry, maybe he was already pure again. So at no single moment did he have awareness of definite impurity, and a קרבן normally requires that kind of awareness.

keyTerms.meaning: Why?
Uncertain awareness: awareness of impurity that is only possible, not definite

phrases.english: But why is he liable?
It is only uncertain awareness!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the first תנא's ruling quoted in step 4.
steps.kashyaTarget: The first תנא's ruling that he is liable even though he purified between the two paths.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Each entry, taken by itself, involved only a doubt of impurity, and a קרבן requires awareness of definite impurity.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: here uncertain awareness was treated as full awareness
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן answers that in this case, the חכמים treated uncertain awareness like real awareness.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: Here they treated uncertain awareness like awareness.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן answers the question by saying this case is a special one, where a doubt counts as knowledge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Taken together, it is certain that one of his two entries was in a state of impurity. Because of that, the doubtful awareness at each entry was counted as real awareness, and he is liable.

keyTerms.meaning: Here they made (treated it as)
Like awareness

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
Here they made uncertain awareness like awareness.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: כָּאן עָשׂוּ סְפֵק יְדִיעָה כִּידִיעָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 5.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Exception: a special rule for this case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Uncertain awareness is never enough to make him liable for a קרבן.
steps.terutzMaskana: In this case, uncertain awareness is treated like real awareness.

steps.title: ריש לקיש: this follows רבי ישמעאל
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש gives a different answer: the ברייתא follows רבי ישמעאל, who does not require awareness at the beginning at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said: Whose view is this? It is רבי ישמעאל's, who said that we do not need awareness at the beginning.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש answers the same question in a different way, by naming which תנא the ברייתא follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן made a special exception for this case. ריש לקיש instead says this ברייתא follows רבי ישמעאל, who does not require any awareness before entering. With that, the problem of uncertain awareness at the beginning disappears.

keyTerms.meaning: Whose view is this?
We do not need
At the beginning, before he entered

steps.whatToRemember: Two answers to why the first תנא says חייב: רבי יוחנן says that here uncertain awareness counts as awareness, and ריש לקיש says the ברייתא follows רבי ישמעאל, who needs no awareness at the beginning.

phrases.english: And Reish Lakish said:
Whose is this? It is Rabbi Yishmael's,
who said: We do not need awareness at the beginning.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second answer to the challenge in step 5, different from רבי יוחנן's answer.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Attributing the ברייתא to a specific תנא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Awareness at the beginning is required, so a doubt at the beginning should exempt him.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא follows רבי ישמעאל, who does not require awareness at the beginning.

steps.title: Each אמורא seems to contradict himself
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא announces a contradiction between רבי יוחנן and his own other statement, and between ריש לקיש and his own other statement.
steps.simpleTranslation: And one can point out a contradiction between one statement of רבי יוחנן and another statement of רבי יוחנן, and between one statement of ריש לקיש and another statement of ריש לקיש.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its next move. It announces that both רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש seem to say opposite things in two different places, and the source comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Just before this, רבי יוחנן treated uncertain awareness like real awareness. ריש לקיש did not, since he needed רבי ישמעאל instead. The גמרא is about to show a case where each of them seems to hold the reverse.

keyTerms.meaning: And one can point out a contradiction (literally, 'throw' one source against another)
Against (short for על ד־)

phrases.english: And one can contrast Rabbi Yoḥanan against Rabbi Yoḥanan,
phrases.notes: The first one is his statement from just before, where he said the חכמים treated uncertain awareness like real awareness.

phrases.english: and contrast Reish Lakish against Reish Lakish.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the two answers given in steps 6 and 7 by claiming each אמורא is inconsistent.
steps.kashyaTarget: The consistency of רבי יוחנן's answer (step 6) and ריש לקיש's answer (step 7).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Each Amora's view on uncertain awareness here will seem to be the reverse of his view in another place.

steps.title: The ברייתא about eating possible forbidden fat twice
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא records a dispute. רבי says a person who twice ate possible חלב, and became aware after each time, brings an אשם תלוי for each one. רבי שמעון says he brings only one.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is taught in a ברייתא: someone ate food that might have been חלב and found out, then ate food that might have been חלב again and found out. רבי says: just as he would bring a חטאת for each eating, he also brings an אשם תלוי for each eating. רבי שמעון בן יהודה and רבי אלעזר son of רבי שמעון said in the name of רבי שמעון: he brings only one אשם תלוי, because the פסוק says 'for his mistake that he mistakenly did.' The Torah included many mistakes in one אשם תלוי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the source behind the contradiction. It is a ברייתא where רבי and רבי שמעון argue over how many אשם תלוי offerings someone brings after two uncertain eatings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי, the awareness of doubt between the two eatings splits them into two separate cases, so each one needs its own אשם תלוי. רבי שמעון learns from the פסוק that one אשם תלוי covers many mistakes. The key question for the next steps is what רבי meant by comparing this to חטאת.

keyTerms.meaning: Food that may or may not have been forbidden fat
Provisional guilt-offering, brought when one is unsure whether he sinned
Sin-offering, brought when one definitely sinned by mistake
An unintentional sin, a mistake

phrases.english: As it is taught in a baraita:
He ate possible forbidden fat and became aware,
then ate possible forbidden fat again and became aware.
Rabbi says:

phrases.aramaic: כְּשֵׁם שֶׁמֵּבִיא חַטָּאת עַל כׇּל אֶחָד וְאֶחָד,
phrases.english: Just as he brings a sin-offering for each and every one,

phrases.aramaic: כָּךְ מֵבִיא אָשָׁם תָּלוּי עַל כׇּל אֶחָד וְאֶחָד.
phrases.english: so too he brings a provisional guilt-offering for each and every one.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יְהוּדָה וְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Yehuda and Rabbi Elazar, son of Rabbi Shimon,
said in the name of Rabbi Shimon:

phrases.aramaic: אֵינוֹ מֵבִיא אֶלָּא אָשָׁם תָּלוּי אֶחָד,
phrases.english: He brings only one provisional guilt-offering,
as it says: "for his mistake that he mistakenly did"
The Torah included many mistakes
in one provisional guilt-offering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source text that both אמוראים interpret, which will expose the contradiction announced in step 8.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי: one brings an אשם תלוי for each uncertain eating separated by awareness. רבי שמעון: only one אשם תלוי for all of them.

steps.title: ריש לקיש: uncertain awareness splits sin-offerings
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש explains that רבי is teaching that awareness of doubt divides the eatings even for חטאות.
steps.simpleTranslation: And ריש לקיש said: here רבי taught that uncertain awareness divides the acts into separate חטאות.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש explains רבי's words in the ברייתא. He says that awareness of doubt is strong enough to split the two eatings into two חטאות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Suppose it later turns out that both foods really were חלב. ריש לקיש says the person brings two חטאות, because the uncertain awareness between them counts like real awareness. But earlier, in step 7, ריש לקיש would not treat uncertain awareness as real awareness. That is the contradiction.

keyTerms.meaning: Awareness of doubt, knowing only that one may have sinned
Divide, split the acts into separate cases each needing its own offering

phrases.english: And Reish Lakish said:
Here Rabbi taught
that uncertain awareness divides the acts for sin-offerings.
phrases.notes: He means that if it later turns out both were surely חלב, he brings two חטאות.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ: כָּאן שָׁנָה רַבִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives ריש לקיש's reading of the ברייתא from step 9, which clashes with his answer in step 7.
steps.raayaObject: That ריש לקיש is inconsistent about uncertain awareness.
steps.raayaSupportSource: His reading of רבי in the ברייתא: uncertain awareness divides for חטאות, which means it counts like real awareness.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: uncertain awareness splits only guilt-offerings
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן explains that רבי's comparison means only this: definite awareness splits חטאות, and uncertain awareness splits אשמות תלויים.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוחנן said: just as definite awareness in general divides the acts into separate חטאות, so uncertain awareness divides the acts into separate אשמות.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן reads רבי's comparison differently. Uncertain awareness splits the eatings only for אשם תלוי, not for חטאת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יוחנן, only definite awareness can divide acts for חטאות. Uncertain awareness is weaker and works only for אשם תלוי. But in step 6, רבי יוחנן said the חכמים treated uncertain awareness like real awareness, so he now seems to contradict himself.

keyTerms.meaning: Definite awareness, knowing for sure that one sinned
In general, in ordinary cases
Guilt-offerings, here meaning אשמות תלויים

steps.whatToRemember: The two אמוראים have switched sides. Here ריש לקיש treats uncertain awareness as strong (it splits חטאות), and רבי יוחנן treats it as weak (it splits only אשמות). In steps 6 and 7 it was the opposite way, so each one seems to contradict himself.
steps.confusionAlert: Both agree that רבי requires a separate אשם תלוי for each eating. They argue only about חטאות: whether, if it later becomes certain that both were חלב, the uncertain awareness also splits them into two חטאות.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
Just as definite awareness in general
divides the acts for sin-offerings,
so too uncertain awareness divides the acts for guilt-offerings.
phrases.notes: The point is that it divides only for guilt-offerings, not for sin-offerings.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: כְּשֵׁם שֶׁיְּדִיעוֹת וַדַּאי בְּעָלְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives רבי יוחנן's competing reading of the same ברייתא, which completes the double contradiction announced in step 8.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי יוחנן is inconsistent about uncertain awareness.
steps.raayaSupportSource: His reading of רבי: uncertain awareness divides only for אשמות and not for חטאות, so it does not count like real awareness. This clashes with his answer in step 6.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן's two statements fit together
steps.stepSummary: There is no contradiction in רבי יוחנן. Awareness of a doubt counts only for טומאת מקדש, because there the awareness is only hinted at in 'ונעלם'. In the rest of the Torah, 'או הודע אליו' requires full awareness.
steps.simpleTranslation: Granted, רבי יוחנן does not contradict himself. Here they made awareness of a doubt count, but not in the whole Torah. Here awareness is not written openly. It is learned only from 'ונעלם'. In the rest of the Torah it is written 'או הודע אליו', so we need full awareness.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the contradiction it raised against רבי יוחנן in step 8. It shows that his two statements deal with two different areas of law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the ברייתא of the two paths, רבי יוחנן said awareness of a doubt is enough. But in the dispute of רבי and רבי שמעון, he said doubtful awareness does not divide חטאות. The answer is that טומאת מקדש is a special case. There the requirement of awareness comes only from a hint ('ונעלם'), so a weaker awareness is enough. Elsewhere the פסוק 'או הודע אליו' openly demands real, full awareness.

keyTerms.meaning: Granted, this part works fine (the 'but' comes next)
Openly, explicitly
'And it is hidden': the word that hints at awareness for טומאת מקדש
'Or it becomes known to him': the פסוק about awareness for a regular חטאת
Full-fledged, certain awareness

steps.whyThisMatters: It sets up a key distinction: טומאת מקדש has softer rules about awareness than the rest of the Torah's חטאות.

phrases.aramaic: בִּשְׁלָמָא דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אַדְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן לָא קַשְׁיָא –
phrases.english: Granted, Rabbi Yoḥanan against Rabbi Yoḥanan is not difficult:
here they made it count,
phrases.notes: He means that for impurity in the מקדש, the חכמים treated awareness of a doubt like real awareness.

phrases.english: but they did not do so in the entire Torah.

phrases.aramaic: הָכָא הוּא דְּלָא כְּתִיבָא יְדִיעָה בְּהֶדְיָא,
phrases.english: It is here that awareness is not written explicitly;
it comes only from 'and it is hidden.'
But they did not do so in the entire Torah,
as it is written: 'Or it becomes known to him.'
So we require full-fledged awareness.

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אַדְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן לָא קַשְׁיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the first half of the contradiction announced in step 8, now that both views of רבי's statement have been laid out.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing between two areas of law (טומאת מקדש versus the rest of the Torah)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יוחנן seems to say awareness of a doubt both counts and does not count.
steps.terutzMaskana: Doubtful awareness counts only for טומאת מקדש, where awareness is merely hinted at. Elsewhere full awareness is required.

steps.title: Why didn't ריש לקיש explain the ברייתא according to רבי?
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש holds that רבי counts awareness of a doubt even for חטאות. So why did he set the ברייתא of the two paths according to רבי ישמעאל instead of רבי?
steps.simpleTranslation: But for ריש לקיש there is a problem. Instead of setting the ברייתא according to רבי ישמעאל, let him set it according to רבי!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to ריש לקיש's side of the contradiction. It asks why he chose רבי ישמעאל when רבי would have fit the ברייתא well.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 10, ריש לקיש said רבי treats awareness of a doubt as real awareness. That would fully explain the ברייתא of the two paths. Yet in step 7 he explained it through רבי ישמעאל instead. This looks inconsistent, or at least unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: Instead of setting it (explaining a source according to a certain opinion)
Let him set it

phrases.english: But according to Reish Lakish:
instead of setting it according to Rabbi Yishmael,
phrases.notes: 'It' is the ברייתא about the two paths from earlier in the סוגיא.

phrases.english: let him set it according to Rebbi!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from רבי יוחנן's half of the contradiction to ריש לקיש's half.
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's choice to explain the ברייתא according to רבי ישמעאל
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: ריש לקיש's own reading of רבי would explain the ברייתא, so moving to רבי ישמעאל seems inconsistent.

steps.title: ריש לקיש wanted to teach רבי ישמעאל's view
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש chose רבי ישמעאל to teach a new point: רבי ישמעאל requires no awareness at the beginning at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what he teaches us: רבי ישמעאל does not require awareness at the beginning.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that ריש לקיש could have used רבי. He picked רבי ישמעאל on purpose, to teach us something about that opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש does not contradict himself. Choosing רבי ישמעאל was a teaching choice, not a disagreement with his reading of רבי. The new point is that, for רבי ישמעאל, no awareness is needed before the sin.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what he is teaching us
Awareness at the beginning, before the forgetting and the sin

phrases.english: This is what he teaches us:

phrases.aramaic: דְּרַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל לָא בָּעֵי יְדִיעָה בַּתְּחִלָּה.
phrases.english: that Rabbi Yishmael does not require awareness at the beginning.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 13.
steps.terutzResolutionType: The choice was made to teach something new
steps.terutzHavaAmina: ריש לקיש should have used רבי, since that fit his own view.
steps.terutzMaskana: He used רבי ישמעאל to show that רבי ישמעאל requires no awareness at the beginning.

steps.title: But that is obvious
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: of course רבי ישמעאל needs no awareness at the beginning. He has no extra פסוק to learn it from, because he uses 'ונעלם' for liability when one forgets he is in the מקדש.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is obvious that he does not require it! He has no extra verses for it, since he uses 'ונעלם' to teach that one is liable for forgetting the מקדש.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer of step 14. Why would ריש לקיש need to teach something so obvious?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The requirement of awareness at the beginning is learned from the word 'ונעלם'. רבי ישמעאל uses that word for something else: liability when a person forgets he is in the מקדש. So with no source left, it seems clear he has no such requirement. Teaching it would add nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: It is obvious, so why teach it?
Extra verses left over to learn from
Forgetting that one is in the מקדש

phrases.english: It is obvious that he does not require it,
since he has no extra verses for it;
'and it is hidden' teaches that one is liable for forgetting the Temple!
phrases.notes: For רבי ישמעאל, this word is already used up teaching this law, so nothing is left to teach awareness.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of step 14 as teaching nothing new.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that ריש לקיש needed to teach רבי ישמעאל's view
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי ישמעאל clearly has no פסוק for awareness, so the point is obvious and needs no teaching.

steps.title: We might have thought רבי ישמעאל has it as a tradition
steps.stepSummary: The point is not obvious. One could think רבי ישמעאל lacks only a פסוק, but still accepts awareness at the beginning as a received tradition. ריש לקיש teaches that he does not require it at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said: when he does not hold it, that is only from verses, but he holds it from tradition. So he teaches us that he does not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the 'it's obvious' objection. Without ריש לקיש's teaching, we could have made a real mistake.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Not having a פסוק for a law does not prove a תנא rejects it. He might know it from a tradition. ריש לקיש shows that רבי ישמעאל truly requires no awareness at the beginning, whether from a פסוק or from tradition.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have thought
Here: a received tradition (not the Talmud)
He does not hold it / he does hold it

steps.whatToRemember: Both contradictions are settled. For רבי יוחנן, doubtful awareness counts only for טומאת מקדש. ריש לקיש explained the ברייתא through רבי ישמעאל to teach that he needs no awareness at the beginning at all, not even from tradition.
steps.confusionAlert: In this line, 'גמרא' does not mean the Talmud. It means a teaching passed down from teacher to student.

phrases.english: You might have said:
when he does not hold it, that is from verses,
but from tradition he does hold it;
so he teaches us that he does not.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the objection of step 15 and closes the discussion.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי ישמעאל might accept awareness at the beginning as a tradition, even without a פסוק.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי ישמעאל does not require awareness at the beginning at all.

steps.title: Hadran — Closing ידיעות הטומאה
steps.stepSummary: The traditional closing line for the second פרק, ידיעות הטומאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, ידיעות הטומאה.
steps.whatsHappening: This is not part of the argument. It is the standard farewell said at the end of a פרק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The הדרן marks that the learning of פרק ידיעות הטומאה is complete. It also expresses the hope of coming back to learn it again.

keyTerms.meaning: We will return to you: the formula that closes a פרק

phrases.english: We will return to you, 'Awarenesses of Impurity'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the פרק after the final discussion.

steps.title: New chapter: two oaths that are really four
steps.stepSummary: The משנה opens the new פרק by listing the four basic forms of a שבועת ביטוי about eating.
steps.simpleTranslation: There are two kinds of oaths, which are really four: 'I swear I will eat' and 'I swear I will not eat' (about the future), 'I swear I ate' and 'I swear I did not eat' (about the past).
steps.whatsHappening: A new פרק starts. The משנה sets up the basic list of oaths that the rest of the פרק will discuss.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'two' are oaths about the future and oaths about the past. Each can be stated positively or negatively, which gives four.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה
An oath
That I will eat (future)
That I ate (past)

steps.whyThisMatters: These four forms are the backbone of the whole פרק. Every later case is one of these four.

phrases.english: MISHNA: Oaths are two, which are four:
"On my oath I will eat" and "that I will not eat,"
"that I ate" and "that I did not eat."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The previous step closed פרק ידיעות הטומאה. This opens a new פרק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There are four basic forms of an oath about eating: future positive, future negative, past positive, past negative.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא: even a tiny bite breaks the oath
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא rules that if someone swore not to eat and then ate any amount at all, he is חייב.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone says 'I swear I will not eat' and then eats even the smallest amount, he is liable. This is רבי עקיבא's view.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a ruling: breaking a 'not eat' oath does not need a minimum amount of food, according to רבי עקיבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually eating laws need a set minimum amount, a כזית. רבי עקיבא says this oath has no minimum: any eating at all counts as breaking it.

keyTerms.meaning: Any amount at all, even a tiny bit
Liable (here, to bring a קרבן)

phrases.aramaic: ״שְׁבוּעָה שֶׁלֹּא אוֹכַל״, וְאָכַל כׇּל שֶׁהוּא – חַיָּיב.
phrases.english: If he said "On my oath I will not eat," and he ate any amount, he is liable.
These are the words of Rabbi Akiva.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁבוּעָה שֶׁלֹּא אוֹכַל וְאָכַל כׇּל שֶׁהוּא חַיָּיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes one of the four oaths just listed and gives a ruling about how much eating breaks it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי עקיבא, one who swore not to eat is חייב for eating any amount.

steps.title: The Rabbis object: no eating law works with a tiny amount
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים challenge רבי עקיבא: where else is someone liable for eating less than a minimum amount?
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to רבי עקיבא: Where do we ever find that a person who eats a tiny amount is liable, that you say this person is liable?
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים push back on רבי עקיבא's ruling by comparing it to every other eating law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Throughout the Torah, eating a forbidden food makes you liable only for a minimum amount. The חכמים argue this oath should follow the same pattern, so a tiny bite should not count.

keyTerms.meaning: Where do we find? (asking for a precedent)
One who eats

phrases.english: They said to Rabbi Akiva:
Where do we find, regarding one who eats any amount,
that he is liable, that this one should be liable?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לוֹ לְרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא הֵיכָן מָצִינוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי עקיבא's ruling in the previous step.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי עקיבא's ruling that any amount of eating breaks the oath.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: No other eating law makes a person liable without a minimum amount, so this one should not either.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא answers: this whole law is already unusual
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא replies that this category has no normal precedent anyway, since here a person brings a קרבן just for speaking.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא said to them: And where do we ever find someone who just speaks and brings a קרבן, the way this person speaks and brings a קרבן?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא answers the חכמים with a question of his own, showing that comparing to other laws does not work here.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every other קרבן comes for an action, but here the person is liable because of his own words. Since the law is unique anyway, it does not have to follow the minimum-amount rule of other eating laws.

keyTerms.meaning: One who speaks
An offering brought to the מקדש
And is it so? (introduces a counter-question)

steps.whatToRemember: רבי עקיבא: a שבועה is a unique law built on speech, so it does not need the usual minimum amount of eating.

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva said to them:

phrases.aramaic: וְכִי הֵיכָן מָצִינוּ בִּמְדַבֵּר וּמֵבִיא קׇרְבָּן
phrases.english: And where do we find one who speaks and brings an offering,
that this one speaks and brings an offering?
phrases.notes: He means: the man only took an oath with his mouth, and yet he brings a קרבן.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָהֶם רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא וְכִי הֵיכָן מָצִינוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the חכמים' challenge from the previous step.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rejecting the comparison: the category is unique, so outside precedents do not apply.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A שבועה about eating should follow the minimum-amount rule of other eating laws.
steps.terutzMaskana: Since liability here comes from speech, a law with no parallel, it need not match other eating laws.

steps.title: Does 'שבועה שאוכל' really mean 'I will eat'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether 'שבועה שאוכל' means 'I will eat', and points to a משנה in נדרים where the same words seem to forbid the food.
steps.simpleTranslation: Are we saying that 'שבועה שאוכל' means 'I will eat'? But here is a contradiction: if someone says 'I swear I won't eat yours', 'I swear I will eat yours', or 'No! I swear I won't eat yours', the food is forbidden to him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins and points out a clash between our משנה and a משנה in נדרים about what the words 'שבועה שאוכל' mean.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה treats 'שבועה שאוכל' as a promise to eat. But the משנה in נדרים lists 'שבועה שאוכל לך' together with the cases that forbid the food, as if it meant 'I won't eat yours'. So which meaning is right?

keyTerms.meaning: Is this to say?
It means; it implies
I will eat (Aramaic)
And raise a contradiction (between two sources)
Forbidden

steps.confusionAlert: The middle case, 'שבועה שאוכל לך', sounds like a promise to eat, yet the משנה in נדרים says the food is forbidden. That surprising result is the whole question.

phrases.english: GEMARA: Is this to say that "that I will eat" means "I will eat"?!
And raise a contradiction:
phrases.notes: The contradiction comes from a משנה in נדרים (16a).

phrases.english: "On my oath I will not eat of yours,"
"On my oath I will eat of yours,"
"Not on my oath that I will not eat of yours" — it is forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the opening list of the משנה and questions the meaning of its wording.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's assumption that 'שבועה שאוכל' means 'I will eat'.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה in נדרים treats the same wording as a vow not to eat, since the food becomes forbidden.

steps.title: אביי: it depends on whether he is being pressed to eat
steps.stepSummary: אביי keeps the plain meaning, 'I will eat', and explains that the משנה in נדרים speaks of someone being pressured to eat.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: Really, it means 'I will eat'. There is no contradiction: here, people are pressing him to eat; there, they are not...
steps.whatsHappening: אביי resolves the clash by saying the two משניות speak about different situations. His sentence continues on the next עמוד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally 'שבועה שאוכל' means 'I will eat', as in our משנה. But when people keep urging someone to eat, 'I swear I'll eat yours!' is said as a refusal, so it forbids the food, as in the משנה in נדרים.

keyTerms.meaning: Actually; really (keeping the original assumption)
It is not difficult; no contradiction
They are pressing him; urging him

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the meaning of an oath can depend on the setting in which it is said, not only on the bare words.

phrases.english: Abaye said: Actually, it means "I will eat";

phrases.aramaic: לָא קַשְׁיָא, כָּאן בִּמְסָרְבִין בּוֹ לֶאֱכוֹל,
phrases.english: it is not difficult: here, it is where they are pressing him to eat,
phrases.notes: 'Here' is the משנה in נדרים, where his words come out as a refusal.

phrases.english: there, it is where they are not

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי לְעוֹלָם דְּאָכֵילְנָא מַשְׁמַע לָא קַשְׁיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in the previous step.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases: two different situations.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'שבועה שאוכל' might always mean 'I won't eat', as the משנה in נדרים seems to show.
steps.terutzMaskana: It usually means 'I will eat'. Only when he is being pressed to eat is it a refusal that forbids the food.
